key_insight: DFT predicts that GeC/ReS₂ favors direct Z-scheme charge transfer, enabling overall photocatalytic water splitting with strain-tunable performance.
engineering_relevance: The heterostructure offers a computational design route toward visible-light-driven hydrogen production through interface engineering and tensile strain.
method: First-principles DFT analysis of structural stability and electronic properties.
Band alignment and Gibbs free-energy comparisons of type-II and Z-scheme pathways.
Evaluation of pH-dependent reactions and strain-dependent solar-to-hydrogen efficiency.
evidence_signal: Calculations predict a 1.38 eV indirect gap, Z-scheme HER feasibility at pH 0–14, light-driven OER at pH 4–14, and solar-to-hydrogen efficiency increasing from 41.40% unstrained to 60.68% at +6% tensile strain.
watch_item: The predicted efficiencies and charge-transfer mechanism require experimental validation, including whether +6% tensile strain can be maintained under operating conditions.
paper_title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
